title: SLO regression and graceful-degradation gaps during cross-region capacity disruption
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2025-03-04 between 15:06 and 15:44 UTC we observed a sustained SLO miss for 99th-percentile inference latency for customers routed to eu-west-1. The incident originated when an IaaS networking maintenance event reduced available GPU capacity in eu-west-1, triggering traffic redistribution. Two gaps amplified impact: 1) our cross-region routing fallback triggered but a mis-specified circuit-breaker policy prevented progressive ramp-up to eu-central-1 (too-strict open threshold), causing a cascade where traffic continued to queue at edge proxies; 2) load-shedding policies prioritized token-based throttles but did not enact graceful-degradation paths (fallback to cached completions / short-answer mode) for product routes, so latency and cost spiked for production tenants.
timeline:
- 15:06 UTC: IaaS scheduled maintenance began, internal capacity alarms fire for eu-west-1.
- 15:08:36 UTC: Autoscaling muted due to per-region quota exhaustion; kube node-group scaling failed with quota error (AWS limit).
- 15:09 UTC: Smart-router began shifting traffic to eu-central-1 and us-west-2. Circuit-breaker entered OPEN state after 30s failure window because the open threshold was configured at 5 consecutive host failures.
- 15:10–15:20 UTC: Edge proxies continued routing some sessions to degraded eu-west-1 endpoints which backpressured the request path; request queuing increased and 99p latency breached SLO (target 300ms, observed 1.8s).
- 15:21 UTC: On-call enabled emergency traffic diversion to a read-only fallback cluster in us-west-2; partial recovery begins.
- 15:44 UTC: Metrics stabilized to within SLO after manual overrides and quota bump; full mitigation completed by 16:10 UTC.
root_cause_analysis: 1) Capacity reduction in eu-west-1 due to provider maintenance. 2) Region-level autoscaling blocked by hard cloud quota (node quota) that prevented rapid capacity replenishment. 3) Circuit-breaker tuning too aggressive: open window thresholds and half-open probe cadence prevented gradual traffic enablement to healthy regions. 4) Load-shedding policy only supported request rejection and token throttles; no structured graceful-degradation (e.g., cached prefix completions, model-size fallback) existed for key product routes. 5) Playbook detection logic did not surface the quota error prominently in incident routing because quota alarms were gated under infra-only signals.
mitigation_taken:
- Emergency traffic diversion to us-west-2 read-only cluster.
- Manual circuit-breaker reset and temporary lowering of open threshold to allow progressive failover.
- Requested quota increase from cloud provider and applied temporary account-level limits workaround.
- Rolled out a short-term routing policy that prioritized user-facing low-latency routes to warm caches.
action_items:
1) Circuit-breaker retuning: change open-window to 60s, reduce consecutive-host failure trigger from 5 to 10, implement exponential half-open probe cadence (owner: Marco Silva, due: 2025-03-19).
2) Add quota-aware autoscaler fallback: when node-group scale fails due to quota, immediately trigger cross-region reroute and page infra team (owner: Priya Menon, due: 2025-03-17).
3) Implement graceful-degradation strategies in router: cached-prefix completions, small-model fallback, and structured short-answer mode for specified product routes (owner: Mei Chen, estimate: 8 pts, due: 2025-04-02).
4) Improve runbooks: surface quota errors as Priority signals, add step-by-step circuit-breaker reset sequence and safe thresholds (owner: Oncall Team, due: 2025-03-12).
5) Add synthetic tests and canary for cross-region failover showing both latency and correctness metrics, run daily against eu-west-1->eu-central-1 path (owner: SRE Platform, due: 2025-03-26).
6) Postmortem follow-up review with product: quantify customer cost impact and proposed billing credits (owner: Nora Gupta, due: 2025-03-23).

verification_criteria:
- Circuit-breaker retune merged and deployed to staging; canary shows successful progressive failover without queuing.
- Graceful-degradation routes implemented for top 5 user-facing endpoints and show <=10% feature degradation with 50% reduction in 99p latency under failover load.
- Quota-aware autoscaler triggers cross-region reroute in simulated quota-failure test.
- Runbook updates published and incident drill completed by SRE within one week.
notes: Priority for next sprint is to land graceful-degradation for product routes before increasing multi-region rollouts. Consider cataloging routes by business criticality so load-shedding targets non-critical workloads first.
